newsitem.title: LEBANON: Mobius says Arab markets must open up fast.
newsitem.headline: Mobius says Arab markets must open up fast.

text.p: Arab capital markets have to open up and liberalise a lot faster if they want to capture a bigger share of global investment, emerging markets guru Mark Mobius told Arab financiers on Thursday.
"I think they have to open up and liberalise a lot faster, particularly those markets like Saudi Arabia which are strong enough to withstand the flows of capital," Mobius said.
"The Saudi market is not open and many of these markets are closed to foreign investors."

Mobius, who is president of Templeton Emerging Markets and co-ordinating manager of funds totalling $12 billion told Reuters after addressing 400 Arab bankers and financiers at a conference in Beirut that he was optimistic about the development of Arab capital markets.
"We think there is a great future in Arab markets," he said. He had made investments in Egypt and Jordan "and maybe Lebanon in the future. It depends on liquidity."
Foreign investment in the region should be a lot bigger.
Arab capital markets were still small both in the context of emerging markets worldwide and in comparison with the region's gross domestic product and gross national product.

"A lot has to be done to grow these (Arab) markets and the way to do it is to establish the right institutions, like good securities commissions to regulate the securities markets, good registration and custodial operations to register shares and computerised stock exchanges which will allow for good liquidity," Mobius said.
"And finally, you have to fully open up these markets to foreign investors," he added.

Mobius said the development of Arab capital markets had an important moral element in its favour in that the Koran, the Moslem holy book, encouraged equity investment rather than investment in interest-bearing instruments.
"These factors are important. Now what's needed is an opening and liberalisation and an aggressive move towards privatisation."
